items.title: Standalone dashboard is container-responsive from 320px through wide desktop
items.precondition: Run the isolated Vite app as owner with the focused Puppeteer runner.
steps: Measure the marked standalone surface at every specified width and breakpoint boundary.
Inspect computed content width, centering, grid columns, gaps, card bounds, and horizontal overflow.
items.expected: Dashboard-owned content is fluid, has no horizontal overflow beyond the 1px tolerance, and is centered with a 1400px maximum width.
items.notes: The runner measures available container width independently of the external AppShell.

items.title: Role permissions and cross-device card ordering are preserved
items.precondition: Deterministic owner, admin, manager, and agent identities are available in localStorage.
steps: Open /dashboard at the role matrix widths.
Compare the rendered card IDs, counts, and DOM order with the permission-derived contract.
items.expected: Eligible roles see Needs Attention first; owner/admin/manager/agent keep their authorized cards and the same ordering at every tested width.
items.evidence: evidence/dashboard-responsive-results.json — owner device matrix plus admin, manager, and agent role matrices
items.notes: No card manifest or permission policy was changed.

items.title: Mobile header and period controls remain complete and operable
items.precondition: Open the owner dashboard with a 320px to 768px available container.
steps: Verify stacked title and controls below 768px and short labels below 480px.
Activate Today and inspect full accessible names and target dimensions.
items.expected: Greeting, date, scope, all four periods, and Open the map remain visible; period targets are at least 40px and the map action is at least 44px.
items.notes: The 479/480 and 767/768 boundaries are explicitly probed.

items.title: Values and details remain contained at mobile width and Extra Large text
items.precondition: Open the owner dashboard at a 320px available container with Extra Large text.
steps: Check every rendered value and card boundary.
Stress the existing value surface with representative long peso and numeric strings without changing application formatters.
items.expected: Values wrap safely without truncation, overlap, clipping, card overflow, or formatter changes.
items.evidence: evidence/dashboard-responsive-results.json — Extra Large matrix and nine-value long-content stress assertion
items.notes: The checked-out park intentionally has no lots, so the runner adds a DOM-only layout stress string to prove the CSS boundary while leaving finance code untouched.

items.title: Touch and keyboard access do not depend on hover
items.precondition: Open the owner dashboard in a 320px coarse-pointer browser context.
steps: Verify every authorized card menu is visibly discoverable and receives focus.
Open all nine menus with Enter, close each with Escape, and focus Open the map.
items.expected: All menus and card actions remain reachable; standalone menus omit Open full screen and retain Collapse/detail actions.
items.notes: Secondary targets meet the 40px floor and the primary map action meets 44px.

items.title: Protected map dashboard-panel behavior is unchanged
items.precondition: Open /map as owner and manager with the panel in docked state.
steps: Check docked geometry and card order, expand to full, then return and hide the panel.
Verify map persistence, full strip height, menu action, and hidden rail geometry.
items.expected: The panel remains 420px docked, uses a 240px map strip when full, preserves map content and manifest order, retains Open full screen, and collapses to a 36px rail.
items.notes: Screenshots were visually inspected; DOM geometry and state checks cover owner and manager consumers.

items.title: Repository type, lint, build, mock, and focused browser gates pass
steps: Run npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.app.json, npm run lint, npm run build, and npm run validate:mock.
Run the focused dashboard responsive browser command and git diff --check.
items.expected: Every command exits zero; focused browser acceptance reports no failures.
items.evidence: Typecheck 0; lint 0 with pre-existing warnings; build 0; validate:mock 0; focused QA 977/977; git diff --check 0
items.notes: validate:mock reports the current intentional empty-park dataset: 0 blocks, lots, contracts, payments, and related rows.

items.title: Repository-wide accessibility regression reaches a pre-existing empty-park fixture incompatibility
items.precondition: Run qa/accessibility-smoke.mjs against the isolated app.
steps: Run the repository accessibility regression.
Record the first failing invariant without altering map data or out-of-scope accessibility code.
items.expected: The broad suite passes, or a pre-existing out-of-scope baseline failure is identified explicitly and waived only for this dashboard-scoped execution.
items.evidence: The first 12 checks pass; the suite then times out at [data-lot-list-action=true]. validate:mock confirms 0 lots, and src/mock/seed-park.ts intentionally returns an empty park when PARK_LAYOUT is absent.
items.notes: This is not a dashboard regression. The focused suite separately proves dashboard keyboard, target, overflow, role, value, and map-panel behavior.
items.waiver: Accepted only for this standalone-dashboard plan because repairing the repository accessibility fixture requires out-of-scope map/mock-data work. The repository-wide suite remains honestly reported as failing and should be repaired by its owning workflow.

items.title: Mutation scope stays inside the approved dashboard boundary
items.precondition: Inspect the final diff against execution baseline 0fc8a80.
steps: Review every changed application and QA file.
Confirm no AppShell, route, map geometry, domain, permission, selector, finance, store schema, dependency, or database file changed.
items.expected: Only dashboard components/types, the focused QA runner, its package script, plan evidence, and the required finalization changelog change.
items.evidence: git status --short and git diff --stat in /tmp/shelter-dashboard-content-responsiveness
items.notes: No dependency or lockfile change is present. CHANGELOG.md is included only because -d requires the patch entry.

items.title: Acceptance artifacts trace the executed contract
steps: Validate test-results.json against the project schema.
Compare test.html byte-for-byte with the approved repository viewer.
items.expected: The JSON rolls up to Passed under the written waiver rule, and the viewer is an exact approved copy.
items.notes: No manual result was fabricated; the one broad-suite failure has explicit evidence and a narrow waiver.
